scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
Apyãwa and Tapirapé identify the people discussed here. Karajá and Kayapó remain distinct peoples; shared land and historic relationships do not make them interchangeable.
The imported 1492 to 1500 polygon is retained as unverified map coverage, not asserted as a precise contemporary settlement boundary or lifetime.
Modern population numbers and land areas are omitted. Sources disagree in their small mid-century population estimates and do not justify a single total.
ISA’s 1996 administrative declaration is distinguished from the 1998 homologation documented by the museum-project authors. No current legal status or pending litigation is inferred.
The NMAI PDF page 9 and the complete short school article were downloaded and read. Only identified passages of the 2020 dissertation and 2024 museum paper were read.
Food and social practices are attributed to the named researcher and informants. Health interpretations are not medical advice and no clinical outcome is asserted.
The two mask catalogues document particular objects. Their manufacture and accession dates remain separate; unnamed makers and incomplete earlier provenance remain unknown.
The UFG appointment was checked against indexed university text after live retrieval timed out. The 2024 museum paper describes planning, not verified completion of a building.
Source checking supports these claims; independent review, depth certification and geometry review remain pending.
